# Label actions by outcome, in sentence case

Destructive and confirming buttons use a verb and noun that name the outcome, and UI text uses sentence case.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Delete project says what will happen; OK and Confirm do not. Sentence case reads faster and keeps capitals for names.

## Prefer

- Use verb plus noun for destructive and confirming actions, such as Delete project.
- Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in buttons, labels, titles, and headings.

## Avoid

- OK, Confirm, Yes, or a bare verb on a destructive action.
- Title Case or all caps in UI labels and headings.

## Use when

- Writing button labels, dialog actions, menu items, or headings.

## Do not use when

- The product or platform has an established, different casing convention; follow the product.

## Sources

- Vercel: Teaching agents product design at Vercel — https://vercel.com/blog/teaching-agents-product-design-at-vercel
- Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Capitalization — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/capitalization

## Check

- Does every destructive action name its verb and object?
- Is UI text in sentence case?
